sections.title: My contribution
paragraphs: I developed the outdoor virtual scene, programmed its visual effects, and designed and helped fabricate the physical installation. I also worked on video editing and project writing. The interior exhibition space and architectural remodeling were developed by my teammates.

sections.title: Real-time technical art
paragraphs: In Unreal Engine, I iterated on Niagara scripts to make fish gather, disperse, blink, and follow spline paths. I also adapted the Ultra Dynamic Sky blueprint and replaced its skybox with imagery made in Stable Diffusion.
For the point-cloud scene, I stored scene-capture depth in the alpha channel and passed it into Niagara to render the landscape as particles.

sections.title: Structure and material decisions
paragraphs: I designed the installation in Rhino and prepared fabrication drawings. Bent steel tubes produced curves that were too rigid, so we switched to hard aluminum wire inside flexible metal tubing. Sheet-metal skin required too much fabrication work and 3D printing was too costly; projection mesh became the final surface.

sections.title: Projection and fabrication
paragraphs: I developed the projected particle imagery in TouchDesigner. Geometry COMP instancing created the particles, while Remap TOP sampled the flow field to update their acceleration and velocity. The resulting motion was projected onto the mesh surface.

sections.title: Project writing and team
paragraphs: I wrote a project study on MR-based immersive cultural-tourism design in Hongfan Village, bringing together the team’s design discussions and implementation work.
Project team: Fenggui Rao, 俞寒译, and 应文康.

sections.title: Physical form and fabrication
paragraphs: The prototype uses a layered, open structure with separate lighting spaces. Cutouts shape the light: small openings reveal point sources, while linear openings work with LED strips. The model combines 5 mm acrylic with mirror paper to sharpen its contours and reflect light between the modules.

sections.title: Lighting controls
paragraphs: A Unity interface uses UniOSC communication to control the prototype. Single-color, rainbow, and breathing modes offer different light behaviors. Touch controls adjust hue, saturation, brightness, and breathing frequency.

sections.title: Motor-driven movement
paragraphs: A motor-driven telescopic mechanism raises and lowers the honeycomb modules. The interface provides up, down, stop, and reset controls. Patterned shells make the changing arrangement and the light passing through it visible together.

sections.title: Programming and testing
paragraphs: The development process connects the control interface, communication code, lighting states, and physical prototype. Mechanical tests informed the clearance between moving modules, while wiring trials addressed cable tangling and unwanted light leakage.
Project team: Fenggui Rao and 俞寒译.
